summary: Frontend-only regression test of alias-host login CORS fix in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js. All 4 scenarios PASS: (1) valid login at alias host importa-projeto.preview.emergentagent.com redirects to /plataforma/studios with 'Bem-vinda, Super Admin' toast, all /api requests go to the alias origin (same-origin), no CORS errors; (2) wrong password at alias host shows 'Credenciais inválidas'; (3) main host REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL login still works (regression OK); (4) /minha-conta shows Registro de acessos populated with new login entries and /plataforma/admins loads the super admins list.
critical_code_review_comments: api.js BACKEND_URL resolution correctly falls back to window.location.origin when page host differs from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL, avoiding cross-origin CORS issues via platform proxy.
The 401 console errors seen on public pages are expected pre-login /api/auth/me probes and are harmless.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The alias-host CORS fix in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js is verified end-to-end. API calls from https://importa-projeto.preview.emergentagent.com now target the same origin. Both alias and main host logins succeed, wrong password message is correct ('Credenciais inválidas'), and login history persists new entries.
rca of the issue: Original bug: alias host served the frontend, but axios used REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL (main host), producing cross-origin /api requests. Platform proxy rewrote Origin header so browser blocked responses with CORS. Fix uses window.location.origin when it differs from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL to keep API calls same-origin. Verified: no CORS errors in console, network shows /api on the current host, session cookie works, /api/auth/me returns 200 (redirect to /plataforma/studios succeeds).
